case_name: I.G. (Karmik) And Others v Prahalad Mani Tripathi
respondent:
Prahalad Mani Tripathi
Supreme Court of India

27 April 2007
Appeal (Civil) 2208 of 2007
The Judgment was delivered by : S. B. Sinha, J.
Leave granted.

facts: The respondent's father Shri Narmadeshwar Mani Tripathi was a constable in Uttar Pradesh Police Service. He died in harness on 2.1.1986. The appellant filed an application for his appointment and disclosed his academic qualification therein.

He was considered for appointment as a Constable but was not found eligible due to not satisfying the physical standard stipulated under the rules. He was appointed as a Peon instead. He accepted the said appointment without any demur whatsoever.

The respondent filed an application before the Uttar Pradesh Services Tribunal, Lucknow praying for his absorption in the post of Constable (M) with consequential benefits from the date of his initial appointment.

A Writ Petition was filed before the High Court questioning the correctness of the order. The High Court declined to interfere therewith despite observing that the right to claim appointment under the dying in harness rules on compassionate ground can be neither used as a devise to seek employment nor it is a new mode of recruitment in Government service nor can be treated as a channel of promotion to higher post.

The respondent accepted the post of Peon without any demur whatsoever and filed an application before the Uttar Pradesh Services Tribunal, Lucknow praying for his absorption in the post of Constable (M) with consequential benefits from the date of his initial appointment.
issues: Whether the respondent was estopped from claiming a higher post after a period of five years.
Whether the rules provided for appointment only to a post for which the candidate possessed the academic and other qualifications.

Whether an employee of a State enjoys a status and whether recruitment of employees of the State is governed by the rules framed under a statute or the proviso appended to Article 309 of the Constitution of India.
Whether public employment is considered to be a wealth and whether it in terms of the constitutional scheme cannot be given on descent.
petitioner_arguments: (i) Respondent having accepted the post of a Peon was estopped from claiming a higher post after a period of five years.
(ii) The rules provided for appointment only to a post for which the candidate possessed the academic and other qualifications.
The Order of the Tribunal and consequently that of the High Court suffers from a manifest error in so far as they failed to take into consideration.
Appointment on compassionate ground is given only for meeting the immediate hardship which is faced by the family by reason of the death of the bread earner.
respondent_arguments: The respondent's father was a constable who died in harness. The respondent filed an application before the Uttar Pradesh Services Tribunal, Lucknow praying for his absorption in the post of Constable (M) with consequential benefits from the date of his initial appointment.

In the facts and circumstances of this case, this Court should not exercise its discretionary jurisdiction under Article 136 of the Constitution of India as not only a prayer was made by the respondent for his appointment to a post which was commensurate with the academic qualifications he possessed, and the Superintendent of Police recommended therefor, but having regard to his alleged deficiencies in physical fitness only, the Police Headquarters directed his appointment only as a peon.
The claim of the person concerned for appointment on compassionate ground is based on the premise that he was dependent on the deceased employee.

Appointment on compassionate ground cannot be claimed as a matter of right. Die-in-Harness Scheme cannot be made applicable to all types of posts irrespective of the nature of service rendered by the deceased employee.
court_reasoning: The Court laid emphasis on the constitutional scheme of equality and the principle that public employment is considered to be a wealth.
The Court carved out an exception in favour of the children or other relatives of the officer who dies or who becomes incapacitated while rendering services in the police department.
The Court stated that once the right is consummated, any further or second consideration for higher post on the ground of compassion would not arise.

The Court held that appointment on compassionate ground cannot be granted to a person other than those for whose benefit the exception has been carved out. Other family members of the deceased employee would not derive any benefit thereunder.
The Court emphasized that public employment is considered to be a wealth and it in terms of the constitutional scheme cannot be given on descent.
The Court stated that appointment on compassionate ground is given only for meeting the immediate hardship which is faced by the family by reason of the death of the bread earner.
holding: The impugned judgment was set aside. The Appeal was allowed. There shall be no order as to costs.
